title: Morpho butterfly — structural color
problem_statement: Pigments fade and need toxic chemistry for vivid colors. The problem is documented and scoped before any solution work begins.
concept: Morpho butterfly wings get their blue from nanoscale structures, not pigment — light interference does the coloring. Structural color never fades and needs no dye chemistry. Crossover note: the power here is the domain transfer — state explicitly what each domain contributes.
novelty_assessment: Color as geometry rather than chemistry.
